transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sonia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lina (CSM), Carlos (Zenith Head of ML), Priya (PM), Marta (Security), Darren (SRE)

Summary (auto): Final POC closeout; performance mostly met targets on Hosted variant, Dedicated shows better 95th latency under load; security team requested KMS/HSM clarifications and audit log retention details; next steps: pricing + SOW, final perf report, security sign-off, exec review.

Topics: 1) Perf results review 2) Success criteria confirmation 3) Security/compliance gaps 4) Commercial closeout steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Sonia (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining on time, uh we wanted to run through the end-of-poc results and make sure we're lined up on the business case and next steps. Carlos you had asked to start with the perf numbers?
[00:12] Carlos (Zenith): yeah thanks, uh yeah, so quick overview - we ran the baseline across your hosted api and then the Dedicated pool for the heavier workloads. the numbers we have here show average latency pretty good, um the 95th for Hosted was about 340ms which is a bit higher than our target, but Dedicated dropped that to 160-170ms under similar load.
[00:31] Ethan (Redwood SE): yep that's consistent with what we saw in the stress tests - Dedicated has reserved GPU capacity which reduces queuing, and our continuous batching behaves nicer with the fixed pool. quick caveat: the Hosted run had some burst traffic from other tenants during one window so that pushed the 95th up, we've annotated the logs.
[00:48] Priya (PM): uh quick q - how repeatable are the Dedicated numbers if we scale sessions to 2x? like what's the degradation curve?
[00:56] Ethan (Redwood SE): good question. at 2x we saw tail increase but still stayed sub-200ms 95th for the core prompt set; at 3x you start to see queuing and then the numbers drift. we included charts in the perf sheet - i'll send the raw output.
[01:13] Marta (Security): can i interrupt - on the security side we still need clarification on encryption at rest for model cache and whether keys can be customer-managed KMS/HSM. you mentioned support for that in the doc but we need specifics for our audit.
[01:27] Sonia (Redwood AE): absolutely, we do support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated and for Hosted we can integrate with a bring-your-own-key model in certain tiers - i will share the security pack. note: the model kv cache is encrypted at rest by default; for full HSM-backed keys that's part of the Private/Tiered offering.
[01:44] Marta (Security): ok that's helpful, can you confirm retention for audit logs - we have a 7 year retention requirement for some events.
[01:51] Lina (CSM): quick note, we have an add-on for extended audit retention; i'll include the SKU in the SOW.
[01:58] Darren (SRE): one more infra q - for the Private deployment do you support air-gapped on-prem install or is there a control plane dependency?
[02:06] Ethan (Redwood SE): Private can be air-gapped with our on-prem bundle, but there are two deployment modes: fully air-gapped (we hand over the cluster and it's customer-managed) or VPC-connected where control plane talks to our orchestration; both have differing levels of telemetry and auto-updates. for audit we can provide local log shipping into your SIEM.
[02:27] Carlos (Zenith): great. ok back to business case, Priya and i compared expected cost per thousand tokens. Hosted baseline came in about $X per 1k, Dedicated amortizes lower at scale. the critical success criteria we want to confirm: (1) 95th latency under 200ms for our core 70% of traffic, (2) accuracy/regression on our eval prompts within +/- 2% of baseline, (3) security sign-off on KMS + audit logs, (4) integration with SSO (SAML) and RBAC. can we confirm those?
[02:58] Sonia (Redwood AE): yes those look reasonable. i would add an operational criteria - we want error rate under 0.5% and stable throughput for peak campaign windows; we can map that to the SLA in the SOW.
[03:12] Priya (PM): on the accuracy item, we saw one class of prompts where the new quantized model produced slightly different completions, about a 3% delta on our scoring metric; is there any way to tune?
[03:23] Ethan (Redwood SE): yeah that was expected - quantization profiles can change some output. we tried a mixed-precision config which reduced the delta to ~1.2% but increased token cost a bit. suggestion: keep Dedicated with quantization profile B for the pilot and run a small eval set in production to monitor.
[03:40] Carlos (Zenith): that trade-off is OK if the accuracy stays within 2% and cost doesn't blow up. do you have exact numbers for the cost delta?
[03:47] Ethan (Redwood SE): yes - in the perf spreadsheet there is a column labeled "quant tradeoff"; rough numbers: profile A (aggressive quant) saves ~32% in token compute, profile B saves ~18% and gives better fidelity. we'll attach the per-run cost calc.
[04:03] Sonia (Redwood AE): ok let's surface blockers - Marta, you sounded like you had two open items for Private deployment?
[04:10] Marta (Security): two things: (1) need a formal attestation for SOC2 coverage and the subservice orgs used in Hosted; (2) for Private, we need to ensure the KMS integration meets our key custody policy; specifically HSM-backed keys or proof of key separation. if Private can't provide HSM we might have to require a dedicated HSM in our environment.
[04:28] Sonia (Redwood AE): understood - we have an SOC2 pack and we can provide the subservice org list; for KMS we support customer-managed keys and we can offer guidance for HSM integration on-prem. i'll get the security pack and we'll note the HSM path as a follow-up.
[04:41] Marta (Security): and audit log retention, reminder: we have regs that want 7 year retention for some events.
[04:48] Ethan (Redwood SE): default is 90 days for the hosted telemetry, but with the extended retention add-on we can push to multi-year; for Private it's customer-controlled entirely.
[04:58] Priya (PM): on timeline, if we get SOW and pricing this week and security sign-off early next week, could we convert pilot into a 3-month dedicated pilot starting mid-April?
[05:08] Sonia (Redwood AE): yes that's feasible, provided the exec sign-off and budget commit - we can target April 15 start for Dedicated pilot.
[05:14] Carlos (Zenith): good. any open commercial concerns? i think pricing looked ok but we wanted a final comparison table for Hosted vs Dedicated - OPEX and uplift for extended audit.
[05:24] Sonia (Redwood AE): we'll include a comparison table in the SOW; the SOW will show per-token pricing, reserved capacity commit options, and add-on SKUs for audit retention and premium SLA.
[05:33] Darren (SRE): small note on integration - SSO and RBAC: do you provide SCIM for user provisioning?
[05:38] Ethan (Redwood SE): yes SCIM supported; SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC at route/role level. also we have audit trails per request.
[05:48] Priya (PM): ok great. let's talk risk: what would cause this to not convert to paid? Marta?
[05:54] Marta (Security): major blockers are if HSM cannot be supported or if audit retention can't be met in Hosted and Private route is not feasible in timeline. also any unacceptable data residency gaps.
[06:04] Sonia (Redwood AE): noted. mitigation: we can offer a Dedicated isolated pool while security continues Private evaluation. that gives you the perf and isolation needs and lets security run the deeper assessment.
[06:16] Carlos (Zenith): that is acceptable. one more thing - we saw a flake in the prefix cache where some session states weren't persisted across node failover during one test. is that something we should worry about in production?
[06:29] Ethan (Redwood SE): we investigated - that was a mis-config in one of the test harness nodes and we repro'd a failover case; we patched the runtime to avoid the KV cache write ordering issue. we'll include the incident note and the fix in the perf artifacts.
[06:44] Priya (PM): sounds good. ok so to close out: can we confirm the final success criteria language so stakeholders agree?
[06:52] Carlos (Zenith): reading out - "POC success if: (A) 95th percentile latency < 200ms for core prompt set under expected peak load, (B) end-to-end error rate < 0.5%, (C) accuracy/regression within +/- 2% on eval set, (D) security sign-off on KMS/audit/SSO." is that acceptable?
[07:09] Sonia (Redwood AE): yes, i'll formalize that in the SOW.
[07:13] Priya (PM): and stakeholder list for exec sign-off? carlos, priy a, marta, and the CFO will be pulled in.
[07:20] Carlos (Zenith): yep i'll loop finance once you send final pricing.
[07:24] Sonia (Redwood AE): ok next steps recap: i will send SOW + pricing, ethan sends perf artifacts, lina will attach the extended audit SKU and onboarding timeline, marta will review security docs. can we agree to reconvene after the SOW is shared? maybe a short exec review the week of April 6?
[07:39] Carlos (Zenith): yes that works.
[07:41] Ethan (Redwood SE): i'll also include the raw benchmark scripts and the config used, so you can re-run if needed.
[07:47] Lina (CSM): and i'll include onboarding steps, common gotchas, and a recommended rollout plan for the 3-month pilot.
[07:55] Priya (PM): great. last thing - any remaining questions from Redwood side?
[07:59] Sonia (Redwood AE): none here. thanks everyone, we'll follow up on the action items.
[08:04] Carlos (Zenith): thanks all. bye.

Notes: transcript has some auto-caption artifacts; speakers sometimes abbreviated. References shared: perf spreadsheet (drive link), SOC2 pack (link), SOW template (link).
